summary.one_liner: Apache SpamAssassin is an open-source anti-spam mail filter that scores email using heuristic, Bayesian, and blocklist-based tests so other tools can act on the result.
summary.what_it_does: It examines each email's headers and body text with a scoring framework and plugins, assigning a score that indicates how likely the message is spam. The distribution includes the spamassassin command-line tool, the Mail::SpamAssassin Perl module set for use in SMTP or POP/IMAP proxies, and spamd/spamc, a persistent daemon and lightweight C client for high-volume mail. It has a Bayesian classifier trained with sa-learn, supports DNS blocklists, and includes plugins to report spam to Pyzor, DCC, and Vipul's Razor. It also has an automatic sender reputation system (use_txrep). It does not delete, route, or bounce mail; an external program must act on the score.
use_cases: filter spam at the mail server
classify incoming email as spam or ham
train a Bayesian spam filter on my own mail
run spam scanning for high-volume mail with a daemon
report spam to collaborative filtering databases
tag spam headers for a mail client to sort
how_to_run: See the INSTALL file in the repository for installation instructions
Run spamassassin on a message from the command line to score it
Start spamd as a persistent daemon and call it with spamc
Use sa-update to download updated rulesets
notable: Scoring framework rather than a yes/no verdict, so an external tool decides routing
Persistent spamd daemon plus lightweight spamc client avoids forking Perl per message
Bayesian filter that learns from your own spam and ham folders
Plugin-based architecture with configurable .pre and .cf files
Part of the Apache Software Foundation
caveats: Not a mail router: it does not delete, move, or bounce spam by itself
DCC and MAPS are disabled by default because they depend on non-open-source or commercial services; some plugins and TextCat are disabled for speed
Upgrading across major versions requires reading the UPGRADE notes for incompatible changes
